summary: Federal/California Title V operating permits generally apply to major sources and specified categories. EPA states that a major source has actual or potential emissions at or above the major-source threshold: default 100 tons/year for any air pollutant, lower nonattainment thresholds for the nonattainment pollutant, and 10 tons/year for a single HAP or 25 tons/year for combined HAPs. CARB states California air districts implement Title V programs and that applications generally are required from any CAA “major source,” Title IV acid-rain affected source, CAA section 129 solid-waste incinerator, or EPA-designated source category. The project facts only identify storage of 60 gallons of flammable solvent at a coating shop and a coating/paint operation, with no location/air district, solvent composition/VOC-HAP content, annual throughput, emissions controls, hours, or facility-wide potential-to-emit. Therefore Title V applicability is indeterminate; based on volume alone, 60 gal stored solvent does not establish PTE at Title V major-source thresholds. Resolve county/air district and calculate facility-wide PTE for VOC/NOx/other regulated pollutants and single/aggregate HAPs, including any lower ozone nonattainment VOC/NOx thresholds and district-specific Title V rule.
title: H-AIR-TITLE-V: Title V applicability cannot be determined from provided facts; 60 gal solvent/coating shop is not enough by itself to show major-source status
